questions.desired_improvement: Resolve the explicitly stated planar (1,1,2)-terminal case with an exact polynomial-time algorithm; randomized polynomial time with a standard per-instance success probability of at least 2/3 qualifies.
questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Bentert et al. (ICALP 2024), Theorem 1: planar Two-Sets Cut-Uncut is solvable by a one-sided-error randomized algorithm in 2^(|S|+|T|) n^O(1) time, but the paper explicitly leaves the three-set planar case with two singleton sets and one two-vertex set open. Fixed-k planar Multiway Cut is polynomial, but it does not impose this uncut connectivity constraint.
questions.forecast_statement: I expect this exact planar three-set case to receive a correct polynomial-time algorithm by the deadline, but regard that outlook as highly uncertain.

items: G is a finite simple undirected planar graph, given without requiring a fixed embedding.
S1={s}, S2={t}, and S3={a,b} are pairwise disjoint; all edge deletion costs are one.
A feasible edge set F leaves s, t, and the connected component containing a and b in three pairwise distinct connected components of G-F; a and b must remain connected.
The objective is to minimize |F|; infeasible instances must be detected.
The event concerns an exact algorithm, not a heuristic, approximation, empirical implementation, or the general nonplanar problem.

questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Two independent reviewers inspect the dated primary source and full proof/algorithm against every frozen assumption. A mismatched graph class, terminal pattern, weighted variant only, or relaxation is not a match. A proof of infeasibility handling and exactness is required. A search miss is not a negative; if no matching source is found by deadline, record INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE unless the separately documented source-coverage review supports an explicit unresolved-at-horizon record.
questions.problem_statement: For an unweighted planar graph G and pairwise disjoint terminal sets S1={s}, S2={t}, S3={a,b}, can the minimum number of edges whose deletion separates every pair of distinct terminal sets while keeping the two terminals in S3 connected be computed in polynomial time?
questions.required_evidence_standard: A dated peer-reviewed article or public preprint containing a complete mathematical algorithm and correctness proof; two independent human reviewers must agree after checking the formal problem statement and proof. LLM review is not an independent reviewer.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2030-12-31, a publicly accessible primary theorem gives an exact polynomial-time algorithm for the specified planar unweighted Three-Sets Cut-Uncut problem, with runtime polynomial in |V(G)|+|E(G)| and success probability at least 2/3 on every input if randomized. The algorithm must either return the optimum cut size and a realizing edge set or correctly report infeasibility. A special case, approximation, or algorithm that drops the requirement that a and b remain connected does not count.

questions.desired_improvement: Improve the current tilde-O(n^(14/3)) exponent to an exact O(n^4 polylog n) algorithm, matching the exponent of the conditional n^(4-o(1)) lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors.
questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Bringmann, Künnemann, and Nusser give a tilde-O(n^(14/3)) algorithm and a conditional n^(4-o(1)) lower bound under SETH. The exact 2D discrete problem remains between these exponents in the audited sources. The 2025 SoCG result improves one-dimensional translation/scaling variants and uses the known offline grid-reachability routine; it does not establish the 2D discrete event.
questions.forecast_statement: I judge an O(n^4 polylog n) exact algorithm for the unrestricted 2D discrete translation problem unlikely by the deadline.

items: Both input curves have n vertices in R^2; the translation is unrestricted in R^2.
The endpoint is the exact discrete Frechet distance value, not only a fixed-threshold decision problem unless the source proves the stated value bound.

The result must state its computational and arithmetic model; independent adjudication checks material comparability with the exact models used by the baseline papers rather than assuming all real-RAM/algebraic conventions are interchangeable.
No input restrictions beyond those in the cited baseline are allowed.

questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Two independent reviewers verify the source's problem variant, dimension, exactness, model, and full runtime derivation. The event is achieved only if the theorem yields O(n^4 log^C n) for a fixed C. A later conditional lower bound alone does not achieve the event. No matching result by the deadline is not a verified negative without the coverage protocol; otherwise retain INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
questions.problem_statement: Can the exact discrete Frechet distance under translation between two n-vertex polygonal curves in the Euclidean plane be computed in O(n^4 polylog n) worst-case time under computation-model and arithmetic assumptions explicitly shown to be comparable to the published bounds?
questions.required_evidence_standard: Public peer-reviewed or preprint theorem with complete algorithm and asymptotic proof, independently checked by two human reviewers. Benchmark speed is irrelevant to this theorem event.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2031-10-16, a public primary source proves an exact worst-case O(n^4 log^C n) algorithm for computing discrete Frechet distance under translation for two planar polygonal curves of n vertices each, for some fixed constant C. The theorem must state its computation model and arithmetic assumptions, and an independent reviewer must verify that they are no stronger in a material way than those underlying the cited baseline bounds; if comparability is unclear, the event is unresolved. A decision algorithm qualifies only if a stated reduction yields the same bound for exact value computation. Approximation, one-dimensional curves, continuous Frechet distance, or a restricted input family does not count.

questions.desired_improvement: Remove the high-girth hypothesis from the cited 3k-round upper bound without worsening its asymptotic approximation ratio or model.
questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Lenzen and Wenning (SSS 2024; arXiv 2024) prove a 3k-round O(k+f(k)^(k/(k+1))) approximation for k-hop dominating set under girth at least 4k+3 and k-hop expansion at most f(k), with upper bounds in the port-numbering model with small messages. They explicitly ask whether the high-girth restriction is an artefact or the bound extends to all graphs of bounded k-hop expansion.
questions.forecast_statement: I consider removal of the high-girth restriction at the same bound unlikely by the deadline, while recognizing that the question is explicit and technically active.

items: k-hop domination means every vertex is at graph distance at most k from a selected vertex; objective is minimum cardinality.
The graph family has the cited k-hop expansion bound f(k), interpreted using the shallow-minor/contraction density definition in the primary source.
The algorithm operates in the source's deterministic port-numbering model with small messages; for each fixed k the 3k+O(1) round limit is constant in n.
No minimum-girth condition or other omitted structural restriction is allowed.
The approximation factor must be O(k+f(k)^(k/(k+1))) with a universal hidden constant; it cannot hide dependence on n or girth.

questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Two independent reviewers check the algorithm model, round count, approximation factor, expansion definition, and absence of any girth condition in the theorem hypotheses. A theorem for a narrower class or with weaker ratio is partial progress only. A search miss is not a negative; absent complete source coverage use INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
questions.problem_statement: Can the constant-round k-hop dominating-set approximation bound proved for high-girth graphs of bounded k-hop expansion be achieved on all graphs of the same bounded k-hop expansion, without a girth assumption?
questions.required_evidence_standard: Dated public primary theorem and full proof, independently checked by two human reviewers; simulations and benchmark evidence do not qualify.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2031-10-16, a public primary theorem gives a deterministic LOCAL/port-numbering algorithm using at most 3k+O(1) rounds and small messages which, for every fixed integer k>=1 and every graph family whose k-hop expansion is bounded by f(k), computes a k-hop dominating set of size at most C*(k+f(k)^(k/(k+1)))*OPT on every graph in the family, for a universal constant C, with no girth assumption. A restricted girth class, randomized-only theorem, or asymptotically worse ratio does not count.

questions.desired_improvement: Reach the MAX CUT α_GW approximation ratio for unrestricted unweighted MAX BISECTION, with an exact theorem and polynomial-time algorithm.
questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Austrin–Benabbas–Georgiou establish the approximately 0.8776 line of algorithms; Brakensiek et al. (SODA 2026) retain the α_GW question as open and prove that the ε-uncorrelated Basic-SDP two-stage paradigm alone cannot reach α_GW (their gap is below 0.87853). That is a limitation of this paradigm, not an impossibility for all algorithms.
questions.forecast_statement: I judge an unrestricted α_GW guarantee for MAX BISECTION by the deadline highly uncertain, with a directional lean that it will not be established by then: the latest primary result blocks an influential route, but leaves other algorithmic paradigms open.

items: Input is a finite unweighted undirected graph with even vertex count; a feasible bisection has equal-size sides.
The guarantee is worst-case over all such input graphs and is an approximation guarantee for the produced bisection, not an SDP value bound.
The approximation ratio is at least the conventional α_GW constant; no Unique Games assumption is allowed for the algorithmic upper bound.
A randomized algorithm may state the ratio in expectation, but must define that convention explicitly.

questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Two independent reviewers compare the full theorem, graph scope, bisection constraint, approximation ratio, runtime, and randomness convention with this frozen event. The SODA 2026 Basic-SDP obstruction alone is not success or refutation of the all-algorithms question.
questions.problem_statement: Does general unweighted MAX BISECTION admit a polynomial-time approximation guarantee at the Goemans–Williamson MAX CUT ratio, under the same worst-case input scope?
questions.required_evidence_standard: Dated primary paper or proceedings article with a complete algorithm and proof; two independent human theorem checks are required.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2031-12-31, a public primary theorem gives a polynomial-time algorithm for MAX BISECTION on every finite unweighted general graph whose expected cut value is at least α_GW times optimum, where α_GW is the standard Goemans–Williamson MAX CUT constant. The theorem must specify the randomized or deterministic guarantee and polynomial running time. A result only for a restricted graph class, an SDP integrality-gap statement, or a ratio strictly below α_GW does not count.

questions.desired_improvement: Achieve explicit near-optimal matching with a fixed n^{1−δ} amortized update-time exponent on unrestricted general graphs.
questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Behnezhad–Ghafari (FOCS 2024) reduce the runtime to a bound parameterized by ORS graph density and state the n^{1−Ω(1)} update-time target as a major open problem. Assadi–Khanna–Kiss (SODA 2025) further make the algorithmic bound depend directly on ORS density, but do not establish a fixed polynomial exponent unconditionally.
questions.forecast_statement: I judge an unconditional fixed-exponent update-time algorithm for explicit near-optimal dynamic matching unlikely by the deadline; recent work has sharpened the ORS reduction but still leaves the extremal density gap central.

items: One edge insertion or deletion is one update; the graph is a general undirected n-vertex graph.
The data structure outputs the matching edges, not only an estimate of matching size.
ε and δ are positive constants independent of n; the update bound is amortized over every prefix or a clearly equivalent standard guarantee.
The adversary model and probability of maintaining a valid (1−ε)-approximation are stated in the theorem.

questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Reviewers verify that the algorithm maintains edges of a valid matching after every update, handles insertions and deletions, uses unrestricted general graphs, and has constants ε,δ independent of n. ORS-conditional bounds do not count unless they imply an unconditional fixed-exponent bound.
questions.problem_statement: Can one maintain an explicit (1−ε)-approximate maximum matching under arbitrary single-edge insertions and deletions in general graphs with a fixed polynomial saving over linear amortized update time?
questions.required_evidence_standard: Primary theorem and full proof in a dated proceedings article or public preprint; independently check the data-structure output and asymptotic bound.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2031-12-31, a public randomized or deterministic algorithm maintains, after every update in a fully dynamic general undirected graph, an explicit matching of size at least (1−ε)·OPT for some fixed constants ε>0 and δ>0, with amortized update time O(n^{1−δ}) and polynomial preprocessing/space. The approximation must hold with high probability over every polynomial-length update sequence under a stated adversary model. A matching-size estimate alone, a bipartite-only result, or n/2^{Ω(√log n)} time without a fixed exponent δ does not count.

questions.desired_improvement: Establish a polynomial lower bound ORS(n,δn)≥n^ε for some fixed positive δ,ε, or a theorem that implies it with exact constants and quantifiers.
questions.existing_strongest_baseline: The SODA 2025 primary paper defines ORS(n,δn) using ordered edge-disjoint linear-size matchings, gives lower bounds n^{Ω(1/log log n)} and upper bounds n^{1−o(1)}, and explicitly calls closing the gap challenging. This structural parameter controls the runtime of the FOCS 2024/SODA 2025 dynamic matching algorithms.
questions.forecast_statement: I judge a fixed polynomial lower bound for ORS(n,δn) unlikely by 2030; the known subpolynomial lower bound reflects a long-standing extremal obstruction, although an improved construction could change the dynamic-matching landscape.

items: Use the SODA 2025 definition of ORS(n,r): edge-disjoint ordered matchings of size r, each induced in the suffix union.
The constants δ and ε are fixed independently of n, and the lower bound holds for infinitely many n.
Any reversal between prefix and suffix conventions must be explicitly proved by reversing the matching order.

questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Two reviewers verify the ordered induced-matching condition, linear size, graph order, constants, and infinitely-many-n quantifier from the proof. The implication to dynamic matching is reported separately and not used as the ORS label.
questions.problem_statement: Does the ordered Ruzsa–Szemerédi parameter have polynomial growth for some fixed linear matching density?
questions.required_evidence_standard: Primary mathematical proof in a dated paper or proceedings version with an explicit asymptotic family or theorem.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2031-12-31, a public theorem proves that there exist constants δ>0 and ε>0 and infinitely many n for which an n-vertex graph has an ordered sequence of at least n^ε edge-disjoint matchings, each of size at least δn, where each matching is induced in the union of itself and all later matchings (equivalently, reverse the ordering convention consistently). A mere n^{o(1)} lower bound, a bound for sublinear-size matchings, or a non-ordered RS construction that does not satisfy the frozen ordered condition does not count.

questions.desired_improvement: Prove a fixed constant ε>0 exponential-base improvement for exact worst-case Subset Sum over O*(2^{n/2}).
questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Horowitz–Sahni meet-in-the-middle uses O*(2^{n/2}); Chen, Jin, Randolph, and Servedio improve this by a polynomial factor, while the ESA 2025 primary paper explicitly says it remains open whether worst-case Subset Sum admits O*(2^{(1/2−ε)n}) for a constant ε>0.
questions.forecast_statement: I judge a fixed exponential-base improvement for worst-case exact Subset Sum unlikely by the deadline: the latest checked work still reports only polynomial-factor savings for the core problem after a half-century of meet-in-the-middle dominance.

items: The problem is exact worst-case Subset Sum with positive integer weights in binary and a target integer.
The running time is measured in a standard word-RAM or circuit-RAM model with polynomial factors in input bit length stated.
ε is a positive constant independent of n; an O*(2^{n/2}/poly(n)) bound is not a fixed exponential-base improvement.
Randomized decision algorithms have worst-case input error at most 1/3; deterministic algorithms qualify directly.

questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Reviewers inspect the full algorithm, correctness, input quantifiers, computational model, exponent, and dependence on bit length. Average-case or Merlin–Arthur results are classified separately as partial progress.
questions.problem_statement: Can worst-case exact Subset Sum be solved with a fixed exponential-base improvement over meet-in-the-middle, rather than only a polynomial-factor saving?
questions.required_evidence_standard: Dated primary paper/proceedings article and a complete mathematical runtime/correctness proof; independently check the exponent and model.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2031-12-31, a public theorem gives an exact randomized or deterministic algorithm for every worst-case instance of Subset Sum on n positive binary-encoded integers and a target, running in O(2^{(1/2−ε)n}·poly(n,L)) time for some fixed ε>0, where L is the maximum input bit length; randomized algorithms must have error at most 1/3 on every input. The algorithm must decide existence exactly up to its stated error. A 2^{n/2}/poly(n) improvement, average-case algorithm, promise-restricted algorithm, or Merlin–Arthur protocol alone does not count.

questions.desired_improvement: Extend the source's FPT feasibility guarantee to exact linear optimization while retaining arbitrary large global coefficients and no new parameter dependence on them.
questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Cslovjecsek et al. (SODA 2024) prove FPT feasibility parameterized by block dimension k and maximum local-block coefficient Δ_D while allowing arbitrary entries in global blocks A_i; they explicitly call extension to optimization an outstanding open problem. The 2026 general 4-block FPT result bounds all input coefficients, so it does not directly settle this unbounded-A_i parameterization.
questions.forecast_statement: I judge the optimization extension by 2030 highly uncertain, with a directional lean toward a theorem appearing: the 2024 paper identifies this as the next natural step, and 2026 structural progress on 4-block programs may provide relevant techniques, but the large-global-coefficient regime remains materially different.

items: Use the SODA 2024 two-stage integer-program form with nonnegative integral variables and block dimension k; rectangular blocks may be padded as in the source.
Local matrices D_i have maximum absolute entry Δ_D; global matrices A_i and linear objective coefficients have arbitrary binary-encoded magnitudes.
Running time is FPT in (k,Δ_D) and polynomial in total input bit length.
Optimization returns an exact optimum, infeasibility, or unboundedness; a feasibility-only theorem does not count.

questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Two reviewers compare the algorithm parameterization and exact two-stage input class. Check separately whether a 4-block theorem assumes a bound on every matrix entry; such a theorem does not imply the frozen result when A_i are unbounded.
questions.problem_statement: Does the FPT feasibility algorithm for two-stage stochastic integer programs with unbounded global-block coefficients extend to exact linear optimization under the same local-coefficient parameterization?
questions.required_evidence_standard: Primary theorem and proof with explicit FPT runtime and optimization/unboundedness semantics; independent check of the reduction from the declared model.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2030-12-31, a public theorem gives an algorithm with running time f(k,Δ_D)·|P|^{O(1)} for exact linear optimization of every two-stage integer program with x,y_i∈Z_{≥0}^k, A_i x + D_i y_i = b_i for i=1,…,m, arbitrary integer global matrices A_i and objective coefficients, and Δ_D=max_i||D_i||∞; the algorithm returns an optimum, reports infeasibility, or correctly detects an unbounded objective. The parameter function may be any computable f, but no dependence on max_i||A_i||∞ may appear outside the input bit length.

questions.desired_improvement: Establish a PTAS-style multiplicative approximation scheme for the 1D shallow-circuit diamond-norm identity-check problem.
questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Bravyi, Parham, and Tran give constant-factor classical algorithms for shallow geometrically local circuits and identify a 1+ε approximation scheme for the identity-check problem as an open question. They show inverse-polynomial additive accuracy is QMA-hard in a constant-depth 1D setting; that does not itself rule out a fixed-ε multiplicative scheme.
questions.forecast_statement: I judge a multiplicative PTAS for this unrestricted constant-depth 1D identity-check target unlikely by 2031; the source already has constant-factor methods and strong precision barriers, but those barriers do not rule out the fixed-ε target.

items: Circuit gates act on neighboring sites of a one-dimensional qubit line and depth is a fixed constant independent of n.
The target is diamond-norm distance between quantum channels, not operator norm, and the approximation is multiplicative.
For every fixed ε>0 the runtime is polynomial in input length; the polynomial degree may depend on ε and depth.
The theorem states the gate precision / computation model and treats zero distance correctly.

questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Two independent reviewers verify norm, channel, circuit locality/depth, multiplicative guarantee, zero case, precision model, and runtime. An additive-hardness statement is not treated as refutation of fixed-ε multiplicative approximation.
questions.problem_statement: Can the diamond-norm distance from a constant-depth 1D geometrically local quantum circuit to the identity channel be approximated within 1+ε in polynomial time for every fixed ε>0?
questions.required_evidence_standard: A complete primary proof or algorithm theorem; independent quantum-complexity reviewer checks the norm conversion and input model.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2031-12-31, a public theorem gives a classical or quantum algorithm which, for every fixed ε>0 and every constant-depth nearest-neighbor circuit U on a 1D line of n qubits, outputs an estimate d_hat of the diamond-norm distance d(U) between the induced unitary channel and the identity channel satisfying d(U)≤d_hat≤(1+ε)d(U), in time polynomial in n and the encoded gate-description length (with degree allowed to depend on fixed depth and ε). The algorithm must handle d(U)=0 exactly or define a valid zero-distance convention. Results only for near-identity circuits, operator norm, a fixed constant factor, or inverse-polynomial additive precision do not count.

questions.desired_improvement: Extend proof-valid approximate GDP filtering through the intermediate q range and exhibit a formally certified privacy bound strictly tighter than the specified RDP baseline on an open parameter region.
questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Tran et al. (2026) show the naive natural f-DP filter can fail under full adaptivity, characterize validity conditions, and give an approximate GDP filter for subsampled Gaussian mechanisms at q<0.2 and q>0.8. This leaves the stated intermediate interval as a theorem-coverage gap in that construction; it is not evidence that all filters fail there.
questions.forecast_statement: I judge substantial progress on a valid intermediate-rate adaptive GDP filter by 2030 plausible but highly uncertain: the 2026 paper supplies a rigorous framework and nontrivial endpoint regimes, while the omitted middle range may reflect a real technical obstacle.

items: Mechanism is the Poisson-subsampled Gaussian mechanism with the adjacency and sampling semantics specified in the theorem.
The adaptive choice of future mechanisms/privacy parameters may depend on all prior outputs, as in the source's full-adaptivity model.
The theorem covers every q∈[0.2,0.8] and states its approximation error explicitly; no claim is made about other mechanisms.
Strict improvement is compared with the standard optimized RDP-to-(ε,δ) conversion for the same parameters on a nonempty open parameter region.

questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Two reviewers check the adaptive model, sampling semantics, complete closed q interval, approximation guarantee, and an explicit analytic comparison with the frozen RDP conversion. Numerical experiments alone are not sufficient.
questions.problem_statement: Can valid approximate Gaussian-DP privacy filters be proved for fully adaptive compositions of Poisson-subsampled Gaussian mechanisms throughout the intermediate sampling-rate interval not covered by the current approximate-filter construction?
questions.required_evidence_standard: Primary theorem/proof in a dated paper; an independent privacy-theory reviewer verifies the filter validity and the strict comparator inequality.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2030-12-31, a public theorem constructs a privacy filter valid under fully adaptive composition for Poisson-subsampled Gaussian mechanisms for every sampling rate q in the closed interval [0.2,0.8], with a stated finite approximation/error guarantee and explicit dependence on the noise multiplier, number of steps, and target privacy parameter. To count, the paper must also prove strict improvement over the frozen RDP-conversion baseline on a nonempty open parameter region within the interval. Merely applying an RDP accountant and relabeling its bound as GDP, or proving validity only for nonadaptive composition, does not count.
